products.superPrompt:
You are an editor of beginner reference material who is precise with Bible references and neutral across Christian traditions. Your goal: write the complete content for "2027 First-Time Reader Plan", a references-only plan for reading the New Testament in 2027, in two visual editions.

BUYER AND JOB
Adults 18-35 new to reading the Bible, often first-time Bible owners. Job: a simple schedule and plain facts about how the Bible is organized, without being told what to believe. One edition is minimal (designed with young men in mind), one soft.

PLAN STRUCTURE (standard, verifiable)
The 27 New Testament books in canonical order, 260 chapters, one chapter each weekday (Monday-Friday) from Monday January 4 to Friday December 31, 2027: exactly 260 weekdays. Weekends are open for catch-up. Friday January 1 is "Orientation day" (read pages 2-6). Chapter counts: Matthew 28, Mark 16, Luke 24, John 21, Acts 28, Romans 16, 1 Corinthians 16, 2 Corinthians 13, Galatians 6, Ephesians 6, Philippians 4, Colossians 4, 1 Thessalonians 5, 2 Thessalonians 3, 1 Timothy 6, 2 Timothy 4, Titus 3, Philemon 1, Hebrews 13, James 5, 1 Peter 5, 2 Peter 3, 1 John 5, 2 John 1, 3 John 1, Jude 1, Revelation 22.
Anchors: Matthew 1 = Mon Jan 4; Mark 1 = Thu Feb 11; Acts 1 = Fri May 7; Romans 1 = Wed Jun 16; Revelation 1 = Thu Dec 2; Revelation 22 = Fri Dec 31.

DELIVERABLE (US Letter 8.5x11 in and A4)
1 Cover: "2027 First-Time Reader Plan" / "The New Testament, one chapter a weekday" / "[YOUR SHOP NAME]".
2 How This Plan Works: one chapter a weekday; weekends free; missed a day? pick up at today's reading or use the weekend; works with any translation; references only.
3 How the Bible Is Organized: two main parts, the Old Testament and the New Testament; traditions differ in which books they include (most Protestant Bibles have 66 books, Catholic Bibles 73, Eastern Orthodox Bibles more), while the 27-book New Testament is shared by all three; Jewish scripture (the Tanakh) contains the same books as the Protestant Old Testament, arranged differently.
4 How to Read a Reference: book, chapter, verse ("John 3:16"); ranges ("Mark 1:1-8"); numbered books ("1 John" is not "John"); chapter and verse numbers were added long after the books were written, to help readers find passages.
5 The New Testament by Type: Gospels (Matthew, Mark, Luke, John); History (Acts); Letters (21: thirteen open with Paul's name; the others are Hebrews, James, 1-2 Peter, 1-3 John, Jude); Apocalyptic (Revelation). Table: book | chapters | one neutral, factual line.
6 Old Testament at a Glance: genre groups (Law, History, Poetry and Wisdom, Prophets) in the 66-book Protestant order, labeled as such, noting that other traditions include and order books differently.
7 Year Tracker: 27 books with one box per chapter (260 boxes).
8-19 Monthly pages, January-December: table Date | Day | Reading | check box; weekend rows shaded "Open / catch-up".
20 Notes: date | reference | notes.
21-22 Undated Version for late starters: Weeks 1-52 x Mon-Fri readings.

EDITIONS (same text)
Minimal: Bone #EDEBE6, Charcoal #232323, Olive #5E6B4E, Slate #6B7A89, Rust #A0522D; Oswald headings, Inter body; square grids, no florals.
Soft: Cream #FBF7F0, Dusty Rose #D8A7A0, Sage #A8B5A0, Warm Taupe #8C7B6B, Ink #3A3A3A; Cormorant Garamond headings, Lato body; thin botanical line accents.

CONTENT RULES
References only: no verse text from any translation. Original, plain, descriptive wording at about an 8th-grade level. Say "traditionally" or "many readers" where traditions differ; never explain what a passage means or take sides on doctrine or authorship.

WHY THIS IS BETTER
A first-timer's pace that fits real weeks, orientation pages most trackers skip, and a minimal edition for buyers who don't want florals.

CONSTRAINTS
No ministry, church, app, publisher or translation brand names; no names of published reading plans; no claims about spiritual, emotional or mental-health outcomes.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Page by page: "=== PAGE [n]: [title] ===", "Layout:" (one line), exact text, monthly tables as pipe tables. End with:
SELF-CHECK (fix any "no"): 260 dated readings; each book's chapters consecutive and in canonical order; all six anchors match; no weekend readings; no verse text; no brand names; no outcome claims; wording neutral and original.

assembly: Run the super prompt. If any self-check item fails, ask the AI to regenerate the monthly tables.

Verify the schedule yourself: 260 readings in total; the six anchors (Matthew 1 Mon Jan 4, Mark 1 Thu Feb 11, Acts 1 Fri May 7, Romans 1 Wed Jun 16, Revelation 1 Thu Dec 2, Revelation 22 Fri Dec 31); chapter counts per book against any printed Bible's table of contents; no weekend readings.

Accuracy and neutrality review (the rights note asks for one): have one or two people who read the Bible, ideally from different traditions, read pages 2-6 and flag anything inaccurate or one-sided. Fix it before designing.

In Canva, create a US Letter design (8.5 x 11 in) for the Minimal edition (Oswald/Inter, Minimal palette) and build the monthly page with Elements > Table (Date | Day | Reading | check). Paste in the content.
Duplicate the design for the Soft edition: swap to Cormorant Garamond/Lato, the Soft palette and thin botanical accents.
Export each edition as PDF Print (300 DPI) in Letter, then Resize (paid plan) or copy into A4 designs and export: 4 PDFs in total.
Create two separate Etsy listings (Minimal, Soft) at the same price with the same number of photos for the style test; on Gumroad, sell one product with both editions.
Make 3 pins per edition with Canva's Pinterest Pin template (1000x1500) and export as PNG.

Write the Etsy listing for my printable "2027 First-Time Reader Plan - [MINIMAL or SOFT] Edition": a references-only plan to read the New Testament in 2027 at one chapter per weekday (Monday Jan 4 to Friday Dec 31, 2027; weekends open for catch-up), with orientation pages (how the Bible is organized, how to read a reference, the New Testament by type, Old Testament at a glance), a 260-box year tracker, 12 monthly checklists, a notes page and an undated weekly version for late starters. 22 pages; US Letter and A4 PDFs. Buyer: adults 18-35 who are new to reading the Bible. [For the Minimal edition add: clean design, no florals.]

Produce:
1. TITLE under 140 characters starting with the buyer's search phrase (for example "Bible Reading Plan 2027" or "New Testament Reading Plan 2027"), then key features. Give 3 options and mark your pick.
2. 13 TAGS, each 20 characters or fewer (show each count), no repeats, covering bible reading plan, 2027, new testament, bible tracker, beginner, printable, and minimalist or aesthetic (match the edition).
3. DESCRIPTION: two-line opener; "What's inside" bullets; "Files and sizes"; "How delivery works" (instant download from Etsy Purchases; nothing ships; print at home); "Good to know" (references only, no scripture text; works with any translation; the 27-book New Testament is shared by Catholic, Orthodox and Protestant Bibles); one line saying AI tools helped draft it and the orientation pages were checked for accuracy; usage terms ([YOUR CHOICE: personal use only, or small groups may print copies]).
4. FAQ with 5 Q&As: Which translation do I need? Is any Bible text included? What if I start late or miss days? Can I print copies for my study group? Refunds (answer: [YOUR REFUND POLICY]).

Rules: no ministry, church, app, publisher, translation or reading-plan brand names (for example, never the names of Bible apps or devotional brands, and never the phrase "One Year Bible"); no claims about spiritual growth, peace, healing or mental health; neutral across Christian traditions; original wording; plain US English.

products.superPrompt:
You are a journal designer and a neutral, careful editor. Your goal: write the complete interior content for an undated, 365-entry Bible reading-notes journal, published as a 6x9 in paperback and sold as a printable PDF, in two matching editions (Minimal and Soft).

BUYER AND JOB
The buyer is a new Bible reader aged 18-35 who prefers writing by hand. They need a simple, neutral place to record what they read, what stood out and their questions, with short orientation pages at the front. It must work with any reading plan, any translation and any pace.

DELIVERABLE: 384 pages, number every page
1 Title: "Reading Notes" / "A 365-entry journal for reading the Bible" / "[YOUR SHOP NAME]".
2 This Journal Belongs To (name, start date).
3 How to Use: one entry per reading; entries are undated, so skipped days don't matter; use any plan or translation; write as much or as little as you like.
4 How the Bible Is Organized: Old and New Testaments; traditions include different books (most Protestant Bibles 66, Catholic Bibles 73, Eastern Orthodox Bibles more); the 27-book New Testament is shared by all three.
5 How to Read a Reference: book, chapter, verse ("John 3:16"), ranges, numbered books.
6 Kinds of Writing You'll Meet: law, history, poetry and wisdom, prophecy, gospels, letters, apocalyptic; one neutral, factual line each.
7-8 Books I've Read: the 66 books in Protestant order with a box each, labeled as that order, plus 7 blank lines headed "Other books in my Bible" (for readers of Catholic or Orthodox Bibles).
9-10 Passages I Want to Return To: reference | entry number | why.
11-12 Questions to Bring to a Study Group, Mentor or Friend: question | reference | answered?
13-14 My Reading Log: date started | plan or approach | date finished.
15 Tips for Writing Notes (neutral and practical: write the reference first, note who is speaking and to whom, mark words to look up, keep questions short).
16 Blank.
17-381 Entry pages, one per page: "No. ____" | "Date ____" | "Passage ____" | "What stood out" (8 lines) | "Questions I have" (5 lines) | "Notes or prayer (optional)" (8 lines) | "Read again? [ ]".
382-384 Notes (lined).

DESIGN
Paperback interior: 6x9 in, no bleed, black ink; 0.75 in margin on both left and right (covers the inside-margin minimum for this page count), 0.5 in top and bottom; writing lines 50% gray, about 0.3 in apart. Printable: US Letter 8.5x11 in and A4, same content. Make the two interiors visibly different, not just the covers: Minimal uses Oswald headings, Inter labels and dot-grid writing areas; Soft uses Cormorant Garamond headings, Lato labels, ruled lines and a small leaf divider. Cover palettes: Minimal Bone #EDEBE6, Charcoal #232323, Olive #5E6B4E, Slate #6B7A89; Soft Cream #FBF7F0, Dusty Rose #D8A7A0, Sage #A8B5A0, Warm Taupe #8C7B6B. Interiors stay grayscale.

CONTENT RULES
Original, plain, warm wording at about an 8th-grade level. No scripture text at all. Prompts must not assume an experience or belief (write "What stood out", not "What did God tell you"). Do not present any journaling method as new, and do not name branded methods.

WHY THIS IS BETTER
It matches the 2027 First-Time Reader Plan in both styles, it is undated so it never expires, and its front pages orient a first-time reader without teaching doctrine.

CONSTRAINTS
No ministry, church, app, publisher, translation or reading-plan brand names. No claims about spiritual, emotional or mental-health outcomes. Neutral across Christian traditions.

OUTPUT FORMAT
Pages 1-16 one by one: "=== PAGE [n]: [title] ===", "Layout:" (one line), exact text. Then ONE entry-page template per edition with exact labels and line counts, then the back pages. End with:
SELF-CHECK (fix any "no"): page total 384 (16 + 365 + 3); no scripture text; no brand names; no outcome claims; prompts neutral; the two interiors differ in typography and writing-area style but share the same wording.
